items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: including Tootsie Mondello, a white saxophone player.

ctx.x: And then Sunday morning, I get home, tell my wife, hey, pay the taxi, I ain't got no money.

Well, look, Tom, now, this is kind of personal. And I want to ask you how you figure this out. And I've known you and I've talked about how you help me and what an important part as we've shown here in talking, your relationship at the Apollo Theater where all the black musicians, all the jazz musicians played, all the black show people played.

Now, we talked about back in Boston, before my time, you were a kid and your recollections with Johnny Hodges and Jefferson Hilton and all the great saxophone players that came out of Boston, including Tootsie Mondello, a white saxophone player. And we've talked about your deep relationship, of the great writer of music, Duke Ellington. How close you were to him and how he trusted you to decipher his scores.
